case_title: Umesh Singh v. State of Bihar
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 rlw s.34; Arms Act s.27
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Section 302 read with Section 34, IPC and Section 27 of the Arms Act
high_court_outcome: Affirmed conviction and sentence in relation to the appellant
offence_finally_established: Murder under Section 302 read with Section 34, IPC
neutral_facts: The prosecution case was that while the deceased was going along with his cousin brother to catch a bus, the accused persons surrounded them and thereafter murdered him by shooting him with a revolver and rifle. The trial court convicted the accused persons under Section 302 read with Section 34, IPC and under Section 27 of the Arms Act. The High Court set aside the conviction and sentence insofar as some accused were concerned but affirmed the conviction and sentence in relation to the appellant. The evidence included eyewitness accounts from multiple witnesses, supported by other witnesses, and the medical evidence regarding the time of death was challenged, with the court preferring ocular evidence over the medical opinion. The accused challenged his conviction and sentence, but the Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, affirming the conviction and sentence.
